PrivacyCz.metaDescription: Data processed by the Czech pages of Apercura: sources, purposes, legal bases, retention, recipients and your rights, including objection (GDPR articles 13, 14 and 21).
PrivacyCz.title: Personal data protection
PrivacyCz.lead: What data the Czech pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Act No. 110/2019 Coll. on personal data processing.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The operator named in the legal information is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about healthcare facilities
body: Data: the name of the facility as it is registered, its kind (general practitioner, pharmacy, home care…), its fields of care, the address and the coordinates of its place of care, and the provider’s telephone number when it is that place’s own, as the National Register of Healthcare Providers (NRPZS) publishes them. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the register publishes them: the provider’s company number (IČO), its registered office or seat, its professional representative, its e-mail address, its data box and its fax. A telephone number that the register gives for more than three places of care is a head office’s and is not shown.
Identifier: the number the register gives each healthcare facility (ZZ_ID), at the end of the page’s address.
Purpose: letting the public find a healthcare facility, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the facility appears in the register. A page disappears after two weekly updates in which the facility is no longer in the register; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the facilities themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they name
body: A Czech page is a healthcare facility, the unit of the register, never a person’s profile. Most practices are run by a sole trader, and their facility is registered under that person’s name (for example “MUDr. Jana Ukázková”): such a page names the person, and is about them.

Only the facility’s registered name is shown, as the register publishes it. Nothing else about the person is collected: no date of birth, no personal identification number, no home address (the register itself does not publish them), no company number, no ratings and no reviews.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from the NRPZS open data, which ÚZIS ČR publishes under CC BY 4.0. The register is kept under §§ 73 to 75 of Act No. 372/2011 Coll. on health services, which make its content public; the publisher’s own note on personal data cites § 73(8), §§ 74 and 75 of that Act and § 16 of Act No. 110/2019 Coll. Places come from RÚIAN (ČÚZK). Each source is reused with its attribution:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which healthcare facilities are where, what care they provide and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by making the register public and publishing it as open data.
Necessity: only the register’s data about the place of care is shown, the data the law makes public anyway; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the register’s fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the register. A provider listed in a public register expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. In 2013, before the GDPR, the Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ) found after an inspection of a doctors’ directory that basic profile data may be published without consent; this notice does not rely on that finding, which is given as context only. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, profession and identifier shown in their space and their claim, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in facilities and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the operator’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

body: The address of every page ends with the ministry’s own code of the place, after a letter naming its list, so a page can be found and checked against the list:
list: /it/struttura/farmacia-esempio-f12345: the ministerial pharmacy code (codice identificativo della farmacia) 12345, after f.
/it/struttura/parafarmacia-esempio-p002112: the parapharmacy’s logistic-site code (codice identificativo del sito logistico) 002112, after p.
/it/struttura/ospedale-esempio-s010030: the facility code of the HSP.11 model (codice struttura) 010030, after s.
The owner’s VAT number (partita IVA) is never read or stored: for a pharmacist working alone, it identifies a person.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the ministry’s lists: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the ministry publishes the corrected list.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A pharmacy’s or a parapharmacy’s name, address or type: ask the region or the local health authority (ASL) that reports it to the Ministry of Health to correct it.
A hospital’s or a clinic’s name, address, type or beds: the region reports them to the ministry every year; a correction appears with the next year’s counts.
Phone and opening hours: the lists publish none; a place adds them by claiming its page.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the updates of the lists. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form, at its address followed by “/rimozione”.
remove.formTitle: Ask for a page to be removed
remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an email address where we can answer you.

ImpressumDe.metaDescription: Legal notice of the German pages of Apercura: the provider, contact, registration and the person responsible for the content (§ 5 DDG, § 18(2) MStV).
ImpressumDe.title: Legal notice
ImpressumDe.lead: Who provides the German pages of Apercura (apercura.org/de), as section 5 of the Digital Services Act (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz, DDG) and section 18(2) of the Interstate Media Treaty (Medienstaatsvertrag, MStV) ask of a website.

provider.heading: Provider (§ 5 DDG)
body: The German pages of Apercura are provided by the entity below. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of the facilities of Germany that patients visit (hospitals, psychiatric hospitals, children’s hospitals, prevention and rehabilitation clinics, and the pharmacies of Thuringia and Brandenburg), built from the directory of hospitals and of prevention and rehabilitation clinics that the statistical offices of the Federation and the Länder publish every year and from the pharmacy lists Thuringia and Brandenburg publish as open data, without advertising, with a space where a facility can complete its own page. Doctors, dentists and the other health professions are not listed. No appointment is booked through Apercura in Germany.

editor.heading: Responsible for the content (§ 18(2) MStV)
body: The person below is responsible for the editorial content the provider publishes. Information a facility adds to its own page is its own responsibility; as a host of information provided by its users, the provider answers for it only under the conditions of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, article 6).

liability.heading: Content of the pages
body: The directory is built from public directories (the statistical offices’ directory of hospitals and rehabilitation clinics, the pharmacy lists of Thuringia and Brandenburg, Destatis’s directory of municipalities). It can be incomplete or out of date: check the information with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The statistical offices’ data is reproduced with its source, as their terms allow; Thuringia’s pharmacy list under the CC BY 4.0 licence, Brandenburg’s under the Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0. The data page lists every source with the attribution it requires.

dispute.heading: Consumer dispute resolution
body: The provider is neither willing nor obliged to take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board (§ 36 VSBG). The service is free of charge.

review.heading: Status of this text
body: This text is a draft, written before the legal entity was set up. It will be reviewed by a lawyer qualified in Germany before the German pages are announced.

PrivacyDe.metaDescription: What data the German pages of Apercura process, where from, why and for how long, and your rights, objection included (GDPR articles 13, 14, 21).
PrivacyDe.title: Privacy
PrivacyDe.lead: What data the German pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Federal Data Protection Act (Bundesdatenschutzgesetz, BDSG).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the name of the hospital, clinic or pharmacy as the directory publishes it, its kind, its departments, whether it takes part in emergency care and at which level, the kind of its operator (public, non-profit or private) and of the facility, its address and its telephone number when it is that facility’s own; for a pharmacy of Thuringia, whether it is a main pharmacy or a branch and how accessible it is. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Never stored, although the sources publish them: the e-mail and web addresses, the name of the operator, the number of beds and the pseudonymous identifier the hospital directory draws anew every year. A telephone number that a source gives for more than three facilities is a head office’s and is not shown. The hospital directory publishes no coordinates: a hospital or clinic is placed at the geographic centre of its municipality, never at its address; a pharmacy is placed at the point its Land publishes.

Identifier: a key that names the source and the facility (for example k0a1b2c3d4e), at the end of the page’s address. The sources publish no national number: for a hospital or clinic the key is derived from its municipality, address and names; for a pharmacy of Thuringia it is the number of its file at the supervising authority.
Purpose: letting the public find a hospital, a clinic or a pharmacy, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.
Retention: as long as the facility appears in its source. A page disappears when an edition of its source no longer lists the facility; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the facilities themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they name
body: A German page is a facility, never a person’s profile: Germany’s registers of doctors and dentists are not open, and no person is listed. A pharmacy belongs to a pharmacist; when its name as the Land publishes it includes the owner’s name, the page shows it, as a professional detail.

Nothing else about any person is collected: no date of birth, no identity or tax number, no private address, no ratings and no reviews. No patient’s data, and no health data, is processed by the directory.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Hospitals and clinics come from the directory of hospitals and of prevention and rehabilitation clinics (Verzeichnis der Krankenhäuser und Vorsorge- oder Rehabilitationseinrichtungen) that the Federal Statistical Office publishes every year on behalf of the statistical offices of the Federation and the Länder; its terms allow reproduction and distribution, even in part, with the source. Pharmacies come from the lists of the supervising authorities of Thuringia (CC BY 4.0) and Brandenburg (Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0); the other Länder publish no current list as open data, so their pharmacies are not listed. Places come from Destatis’s directory of municipalities. Each source is reused with its attribution:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which hospitals, clinics and pharmacies are where, what care they offer and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by publishing these directories.
Necessity: only the facility’s data from the directories is shown, the data they publish anyway, and less of it; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the directories’ fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every edition of the directories. A facility listed in a public directory expects to be found in a directory repeating that information. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set (§ 25(2) TDDDG): the session of signed-in facilities and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: Data is transferred outside the European Union and the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (GDPR article 77), in particular the one of the Land where you live. The data protection conference (Datenschutzkonferenz) lists the authorities of the Federation and the Länder.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the directories never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer qualified in Germany and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

TermsDe.metaDescription: Terms of use of the German pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of hospitals, clinics and pharmacies from public directories, without booking.
TermsDe.title: Terms of use
TermsDe.lead: The rules for using the German pages of Apercura, for the public and for facilities alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the hospitals, psychiatric hospitals, children’s hospitals and prevention and rehabilitation clinics of the statistical offices’ directory, and the pharmacies of Thuringia and Brandenburg. It lists facilities, not doctors. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Germany. It is run by the provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public directories, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement.

The information may be incomplete or out of date (the hospital directory is published once a year), and a hospital or clinic is shown at its municipality, not at its exact address on a map: check the information with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112. Outside surgery hours, the on-call medical service answers at 116 117.

practices.heading: For facilities
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, as the rules on health advertising (Heilmittelwerbegesetz) and the professional codes require.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information facilities add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The statistical offices’ data is reproduced with its source, Thuringia’s pharmacy list under CC BY 4.0, Brandenburg’s under the Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: The governing law and the competent courts will be specified during the legal review; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityDe.metaDescription: Accessibility of the German pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityDe.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityDe.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the German pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: The accessibility regulation for federal information technology (BITV 2.0) binds public bodies, and the Accessibility Strengthening Act (Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz, BFSG) covers services that a free directory is not. Apercura’s provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA (EN 301 549).

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The German pages share the code of the French pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, in German.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

DataDe.metaDescription: Where the German pages of Apercura come from (Destatis, the pharmacy lists of Thuringia and Brandenburg) and how to correct or remove a page.
DataDe.title: Data and sources
DataDe.lead: Every German page is built from public data. Here is where it comes from, under which conditions and attribution, when it was updated, and how to correct or remove a page.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The statistical offices publish the directory of hospitals once a year, the Länder their pharmacy lists when they change; the directory checks them every month and imports a source when it has changed. A page changes only when its facts change in its source.
status.notImported: The German directory has not been imported yet on this site.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: The statistical offices allow the reproduction and distribution of their publications, even in part, with the source; Thuringia publishes its pharmacies under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), Brandenburg under the Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0 (dl-de/by-2-0). Each attribution below is printed word for word.
sources.caption: Data sources of the German directory

de-destatis-khv.use: Hospitals and prevention and rehabilitation clinics: names, kinds, departments, emergency care, kinds of operator, addresses, telephone numbers
de-destatis-khv.frequency: Every year, by the statistical offices

de-destatis-gv.use: Länder, Kreise and municipalities, and the geographic centre of each municipality, where its hospitals and clinics are placed
de-destatis-gv.frequency: Every quarter, by the Federal Statistical Office

de-apo-th.use: Pharmacies of Thuringia: names, main pharmacy or branch, accessibility, addresses and points
de-apo-th.frequency: When it changes, by the Thuringian consumer protection office

de-apo-bb.use: Pharmacies of Brandenburg: names, addresses, telephone numbers and points
de-apo-bb.frequency: Every quarter, by the Brandenburg office for health

sources.conditions: The statistical offices’ editions read: “Vervielfältigung und Verbreitung, auch auszugsweise, mit Quellenangabe gestattet” (reproduction and distribution, even in part, allowed with the source). The data is shown as published, never changed in meaning.
sources.changes: Changes made to the data (dl-de/by-2-0): the pharmacies of hospitals in Brandenburg’s list are left out (they do not serve the public); names and streets are shown as published; every facility is placed in its municipality by its official code or its town’s name; a telephone number shared by more than three facilities is left out.
sources.licenceLink: The Data licence Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0

coverage.heading: Facilities covered
body: Pages are generated for every hospital site and every prevention or rehabilitation clinic of the statistical offices’ directory, and for the public pharmacies of Thuringia and Brandenburg. A hospital whose every department is psychiatric or psychosomatic is listed with the psychiatric hospitals, one whose every department is a children’s one with the children’s hospitals; a site without departments (a day or outpatient clinic) is told by its name. Every department is shown on the page.

Not listed: doctors, dentists, psychotherapists and the other health professions, whose registers are not open; medical care centres (MVZ), nursing homes and hospices; the pharmacies of the other Länder, whose lists are not open data or not current (Saarland’s open list dates from March 2021).

The hospital directory publishes no coordinates: a hospital or clinic is placed at the geographic centre of its municipality (Destatis). Its map position and its distance are those of the municipality, never of its address. Pharmacies are placed at the point their Land publishes.

kinds.DE_HOSPITAL: Hospitals (university hospitals, hospitals of the Länder’s plans, hospitals with or without a care contract, Bundeswehr hospitals)
kinds.DE_PSYCHIATRIC_HOSPITAL: Psychiatric and psychosomatic hospitals, their day and outpatient clinics

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: No source publishes a national number: the address of every page ends with a key that names its source, so a page can be found and checked against it:
list: /de/einrichtung/klinikum-beispiel-k0a1b2c3d4e: a hospital site (k) or a clinic (r) of the statistical offices’ directory, with a key derived from its municipality, address and names. The directory’s own identifier is a pseudonym drawn anew every year, and is not used.

/de/einrichtung/beispiel-apotheke-th420: a pharmacy of Thuringia (th) and the number of its file at the supervising authority; bb: a pharmacy of Brandenburg, with a key derived from its name and address.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the directories: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: Hospitals and clinics: the facility reports the change to the statistical office of its Land, which collects the hospital statistics; the next edition of the directory carries it.

Pharmacies: the owner reports the change to the supervising authority of the Land (in Thuringia the Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz, in Brandenburg the Landesamt für Arbeitsschutz, Verbraucherschutz und Gesundheit).

An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the updates of the directories. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space.

LegalNoticeEs.metaDescription: Aviso legal de las páginas españolas de Apercura: el titular, sus datos de contacto e inscripción, y el responsable de los contenidos (Ley 34/2002, LSSI, artículo 10).
LegalNoticeEs.title: Aviso legal
LegalNoticeEs.lead: Quién gestiona las páginas españolas de Apercura (apercura.org/es), como exige el artículo 10 de la Ley 34/2002, de servicios de la sociedad de la información y de comercio electrónico (LSSI).

provider.heading: Titular
body: Las páginas españolas de Apercura las gestiona la entidad indicada a continuación, que explota el directorio y responde de su contenido.

service.heading: El servicio
body: Un directorio gratuito de los centros sanitarios de España que visitan los pacientes (hospitales, centros de salud y consultorios de la red pública, consultas médicas, consultas de otros profesionales sanitarios, policlínicas, clínicas dentales y farmacias), creado a partir del Registro General de centros, servicios y establecimientos sanitarios (REGCESS) del Ministerio de Sanidad, sin publicidad, con un espacio en el que cada centro puede completar su propia página. En España no se reserva ninguna cita a través de Apercura.

editor.heading: Responsable de los contenidos
body: La persona indicada a continuación es responsable de lo que publica el titular. La información que un centro añade a su propia página es responsabilidad suya; como servicio de alojamiento de datos facilitados por sus usuarios, el titular solo responde de ella en las condiciones del artículo 16 de la Ley 34/2002.

liability.heading: Contenido de las páginas
body: El directorio se crea a partir del REGCESS, que el Ministerio de Sanidad publica cada mes, y de las unidades administrativas y entidades de población del IGN. Puede estar incompleto o desactualizado: compruebe la información con el centro antes de desplazarse. Cada página indica cómo notificar un error.

ip.heading: Código y datos
body: El código fuente de Apercura se publica con la licencia AGPL-3.0. Los datos del REGCESS se reutilizan conforme al aviso legal del Ministerio de Sanidad (Ley 37/2007, sobre reutilización de la información del sector público), citando la fuente y la fecha de su última actualización; los del IGN, con la licencia CC BY 4.0. La página de datos enumera cada fuente con la atribución que exige.

review.heading: Estado de este texto
body: Este texto es un borrador, redactado antes de constituirse la persona jurídica. Lo revisará un abogado colegiado en España antes de que se anuncien las páginas españolas.

PrivacyEs.metaDescription: Datos que tratan las páginas españolas de Apercura: fuentes, finalidades, bases jurídicas, conservación, destinatarios y sus derechos, incluida la oposición (RGPD, artículos 13, 14 y 21; LOPDGDD).
PrivacyEs.title: Privacidad
PrivacyEs.lead: Qué datos tratan las páginas españolas de Apercura, de dónde proceden, para qué, durante cuánto tiempo y quién los trata, y cómo ejercer sus derechos conforme al Reglamento General de Protección de Datos (RGPD) y a la Ley Orgánica 3/2018, de Protección de Datos Personales y garantía de los derechos digitales (LOPDGDD).

controller.heading: Responsable del tratamiento
body: El titular indicado en el aviso legal es el responsable del directorio, de las cuentas de los centros, de las reclamaciones de páginas y de las solicitudes enviadas a través del sitio.

directory.heading: Directorio: datos de los centros sanitarios
body: Datos: el nombre del centro tal como está inscrito, su tipo (centro de salud, clínica dental, farmacia…), su oferta asistencial, si es público o privado, su dirección y municipio, y su número de teléfono cuando es el del propio centro, tal como los publica el Registro General de centros, servicios y establecimientos sanitarios (REGCESS) del Ministerio de Sanidad. Un centro que reclama su página puede añadir una presentación, idiomas, una foto y un horario.

Nunca se almacenan, aunque el registro los publica: el correo electrónico y el fax del centro, su código autonómico y las fechas de sus autorizaciones. Un número de teléfono que el registro da para más de tres centros es el de una sede central y no se muestra. El registro no publica coordenadas: cada centro se sitúa en el núcleo principal de su municipio, nunca en su dirección.
Identificador: el código de centro normalizado (CCN) que el registro asigna a cada centro, al final de la dirección de la página.
Finalidad: permitir al público encontrar un centro sanitario, saber dónde está y cómo contactarlo. Base jurídica: el interés legítimo (artículo 6.1.f del RGPD), ponderado más abajo.

Conservación: mientras el centro figure en el registro. Una página desaparece tras dos actualizaciones en las que el centro ya no figura en el registro; una página retirada tras una oposición no se vuelve a publicar nunca.

Información: los datos no proceden de los propios centros (artículo 14 del RGPD). Escribir a cada uno de ellos supondría un esfuerzo desproporcionado (artículo 14.5.b); este aviso, la página de datos y una nota en cada página hacen pública esta información.

people.heading: Los centros y las personas que nombran
body: Una página española es un centro sanitario, la unidad del registro, nunca el perfil de una persona. Muchas consultas y farmacias pertenecen a un profesional que ejerce por cuenta propia y están inscritas con su nombre (por ejemplo, «Ana María Ejemplo Sanz»): esa página nombra a la persona y se refiere a ella.

Solo se muestra el nombre inscrito del centro, tal como lo publica el registro, con sus datos profesionales: los datos de los empresarios individuales y profesionales liberales referidos a su actividad, cuyo tratamiento presume lícito el artículo 19.3 de la LOPDGDD. No se recoge nada más sobre la persona: ni fecha de nacimiento, ni DNI o NIF, ni más domicilio que el que el registro indica como el del centro, ni valoraciones, ni opiniones.
Cualquier persona a la que se refiera una página puede oponerse a ella en cualquier momento, y la página se retira.

sources.heading: Fuentes
body: Cada página se crea a partir del REGCESS, el registro que el Ministerio de Sanidad lleva conforme al Real Decreto 1277/2003, de autorización de centros sanitarios, y publica cada mes; su aviso legal autoriza la reutilización, comercial o no, citando la fuente y la fecha de la última actualización y sin desnaturalizar los datos (Ley 37/2007). Los lugares proceden del IGN (CC BY 4.0). Cada fuente se reutiliza con su atribución:

balancing.heading: Ponderación del interés legítimo
body: Finalidad: los pacientes necesitan saber qué centros sanitarios hay y dónde, qué atención ofrecen y cómo contactarlos, una necesidad que el Estado ya atiende al llevar el registro y publicarlo.
Necesidad: solo se muestran los datos del registro sobre el centro, los que ya publica; nada de la vida privada, ni valoraciones, ni opiniones.

Equilibrio: un orden neutro, sin publicidad, el mínimo de campos del registro, una oposición que oculta la página de inmediato e impide que vuelva, correcciones en la fuente y páginas que siguen cada actualización del registro. Un centro inscrito en un registro público espera figurar en un directorio que repite esa información. Ponderados estos elementos, prevalece el interés de los pacientes, y cualquier persona a la que se refiera una página puede oponerse sin dar motivos.

accounts.heading: Cuentas de los centros y reclamaciones
body: Datos: dirección de correo electrónico, nombre, contraseña (almacenada cifrada con hash), segundo factor de autenticación, los documentos enviados para reclamar una página (prueba de que el solicitante dirige el centro o actúa en su nombre) y los miembros del equipo.

Finalidades: gestionar la cuenta y comprobar que una página la reclama el centro correcto. Bases jurídicas: la ejecución de las condiciones de uso (artículo 6.1.b) y el interés legítimo en la seguridad del servicio (artículo 6.1.f).
Conservación: la cuenta se conserva hasta que se elimina; los justificantes, cifrados, se borran 30 días después de la decisión.

requests.heading: Notificaciones de errores, oposiciones y solicitudes de contacto
body: Datos: el mensaje, la dirección de correo de contacto cuando se indica y la página de que se trate; en una solicitud «Es mi página», además, el nombre y el número de teléfono. El texto libre se cifra.

Finalidades: corregir errores, aplicar las oposiciones y ayudar a un centro que no puede reclamar su página en línea. Bases jurídicas: el interés legítimo (artículo 6.1.f) y el derecho de oposición (artículo 21).

Conservación: una notificación se elimina 6 meses después de cerrarse, una oposición rechazada un año después de su decisión, una solicitud de contacto 12 meses después del último intercambio. Una vez confirmada una oposición, o cuando el titular de una página reclamada la retira, la página y los datos que le conciernen se eliminan de inmediato, incluida la oposición; solo se conserva un registro de la retirada (el identificador de la página, el país, el motivo, quién la registró y cuándo), para que no se vuelva a publicar nunca. Un titular que retira su página conserva, solo en su cuenta y sin publicarse nunca, el nombre, el tipo y el identificador mostrados en su espacio y su reclamación, hasta que elimina la cuenta.

technical.heading: Datos técnicos y cookies
body: Solo se usan las cookies estrictamente necesarias para el servicio: la sesión de los centros conectados y el idioma elegido. Ninguna cookie publicitaria ni de medición de audiencia, ningún rastreador.

Para limitar los abusos, las direcciones IP se transforman con una función con clave antes de contarse y nunca se almacenan como tales; las sesiones de los centros registran una dirección IP truncada. Las visitas a las páginas reclamadas se cuentan sin cookie ni identificador, y solo las ve el titular de la página.

recipients.heading: Destinatarios y encargados del tratamiento
body: Los datos no se venden ni se alquilan, y nunca se usan con fines publicitarios. Solo los reciben el equipo del titular y los encargados indicados a continuación, cada uno para su parte, con un contrato conforme al artículo 28 del RGPD. Los mapas se cargan desde un servidor de teselas, que recibe la dirección IP del visitante como cualquier sitio web.

transfers.heading: Transferencias fuera de la Unión Europea
body: Los datos solo se transfieren fuera de la Unión Europea y del Espacio Económico Europeo con las garantías del capítulo V del RGPD (una decisión de adecuación o cláusulas contractuales tipo). Cualquier cambio de encargado se anunciará aquí antes de que surta efecto.

automated.heading: Decisiones automatizadas
body: No se toma ninguna decisión sobre usted por medios únicamente automatizados. Una reclamación la decide una persona, que lee sus documentos.

rights.heading: Sus derechos
body: Puede solicitar el acceso a sus datos, su rectificación o supresión, la limitación de su tratamiento, su portabilidad y oponerse a su tratamiento. Escriba a la dirección indicada a continuación; recibirá respuesta en el plazo de un mes.
También puede presentar una reclamación ante la autoridad de control española, la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD): C/ Jorge Juan, 6, 28001 Madrid, www.aepd.es.

objection.heading: Oponerse a una página (artículo 21 del RGPD)
body: Cualquier persona a la que se refiera una página puede oponerse a su publicación en cualquier momento, sin dar motivos. Si la página no está reclamada, basta con un formulario: la página se oculta en cuanto llega la solicitud, se elimina tras una comprobación sencilla y las actualizaciones del registro no la vuelven a publicar. Si está reclamada, su titular la retira desde su espacio.

changes.heading: Actualizaciones de este aviso
body: Este aviso es un borrador. Lo revisarán un abogado colegiado en España y el delegado de protección de datos; cada versión lleva fecha.

PrivacyEs.authorityLink: Presentar una reclamación ante la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos

TermsEs.metaDescription: Condiciones de uso de las páginas españolas de Apercura: un directorio gratuito y factual de centros sanitarios a partir del registro del Ministerio de Sanidad, sin cita en línea.
TermsEs.title: Condiciones de uso
TermsEs.lead: Las reglas de uso de las páginas españolas de Apercura, tanto para el público como para los centros sanitarios.

service.heading: El servicio
body: Apercura enumera gratuitamente los centros sanitarios del registro del Ministerio de Sanidad que visitan los pacientes: hospitales, centros de salud y consultorios de la red pública, consultas médicas, consultas de otros profesionales sanitarios, policlínicas, clínicas dentales y farmacias. Es solo un directorio: en España no se reserva ninguna cita a través de Apercura. Lo gestiona el titular indicado en el aviso legal.
Consultar el directorio no requiere cuenta. Usar el sitio supone aceptar estas condiciones.

content.heading: Qué contienen las páginas
body: Las páginas muestran información factual del registro público, en un orden neutro, sin valoraciones, opiniones, publicidad ni posiciones de pago.

La información puede estar incompleta o desactualizada, y un centro se sitúa en su municipio, no en su dirección exacta en un mapa: compruébela con el centro antes de desplazarse. Cada página indica cómo notificar un error.

health.heading: No es consejo médico
body: Apercura no da consejo médico y no es un servicio de urgencias. En caso de urgencia, llame al 112. Fuera del horario de su centro, el servicio de salud de su comunidad autónoma le indica adónde acudir.

practices.heading: Para los centros sanitarios
body: Reclamar una página es gratuito. Requiere un documento que demuestre que el solicitante dirige el centro o actúa en su nombre, revisado por una persona antes de entregar la página.
El titular de una página es responsable de la información que añade. Debe seguir siendo factual, exacta y actualizada, como exigen las normas sobre publicidad e información sanitaria.

removal.heading: Retirar una página
body: Cualquier persona a la que se refiera una página puede pedir su retirada en cualquier momento: la página de datos explica cómo. Una página reclamada solo puede retirarla su titular.

liability.heading: Responsabilidad
body: El titular hace todo lo posible para que el servicio esté disponible y sea exacto, pero no puede garantizarlo. No es responsable de la información que los centros añaden a sus páginas. Estos límites se precisarán en la revisión jurídica.

ip.heading: Código y datos
body: El código fuente se publica con la licencia AGPL-3.0. Los datos del REGCESS se reutilizan en las condiciones del Ministerio de Sanidad (citando la fuente y la fecha), los del IGN con la licencia CC BY 4.0.

law.heading: Ley aplicable y litigios
body: La ley aplicable y los tribunales competentes se precisarán en la revisión jurídica; se aplican siempre las normas imperativas de protección de los consumidores del país de residencia. En caso de litigio, escriba primero a la dirección de contacto para buscar una solución amistosa.

AccessibilityEs.metaDescription: Accesibilidad de las páginas españolas de Apercura: el objetivo WCAG 2.2 AA, lo que se ha comprobado, lo que falta y cómo comunicar un problema.
AccessibilityEs.title: Accesibilidad
AccessibilityEs.lead: Apercura está pensado para todas las personas, incluidas las mayores y las que tienen baja visión. Esta declaración indica la situación de las páginas españolas.

scope.heading: Ámbito
body: El Real Decreto 1112/2018, sobre accesibilidad de los sitios web y aplicaciones para dispositivos móviles del sector público, obliga a los organismos del sector público, y Apercura no lo es. Aun así, su titular aplica el mismo nivel en todas las páginas: WCAG 2.2, nivel AA (EN 301 549).

status.heading: Situación del sitio
body: Las páginas españolas comparten el código de las páginas francesas y sus pruebas. El sitio cumple parcialmente las WCAG 2.2 AA: se basa en una autoevaluación y en pruebas automatizadas, todavía no en una auditoría completa, que está en curso.

tests.heading: Qué se ha comprobado
list: Comprobaciones automatizadas con axe-core (reglas WCAG 2.0, 2.1 y 2.2, niveles A y AA) en cada tipo de página, en cada versión.
Recorridos solo con teclado, con un foco visible.
Texto de al menos 18 px, zonas táctiles de al menos 44 px, nada que dependa solo del color, sin desplazamiento horizontal a 390 px.

pending.heading: Qué falta por comprobar
list: Una revisión manual con los lectores de pantalla VoiceOver y NVDA, en español.
Una auditoría completa conforme a las WCAG 2.2 AA sobre una muestra de páginas.

feedback.heading: Comunicar un problema
body: Si una página o una función le resulta difícil de usar, escriba a la dirección indicada a continuación: diga qué página y qué le ha bloqueado. Respondemos en el plazo de un mes y, si es necesario, le facilitamos la información en otro formato.

DataEs.metaDescription: De dónde proceden las páginas españolas de Apercura: el registro de centros sanitarios del Ministerio de Sanidad (REGCESS) y el IGN, las fechas de actualización y cómo corregir o retirar una página.
DataEs.title: Datos y fuentes
DataEs.lead: Cada página española se crea a partir de datos públicos. Aquí se indica de dónde proceden, en qué condiciones y con qué atribución, cuándo se actualizaron y cómo corregir o retirar una página.

status.heading: Última actualización
status.body: El Ministerio de Sanidad publica el registro cada mes; el directorio lo comprueba cada semana y lo importa cuando ha cambiado. Una página solo cambia cuando cambian sus datos en el registro.
status.notImported: El directorio español todavía no se ha importado en este sitio.

sources.heading: Fuentes
sources.body: El registro se reutiliza conforme al aviso legal del Ministerio de Sanidad, que autoriza la reutilización, comercial o no, siempre que se cite la fuente y la fecha de la última actualización y no se desnaturalicen los datos (Ley 37/2007); los datos del IGN, con la licencia Creative Commons Reconocimiento 4.0 Internacional (CC BY 4.0). Cada atribución se reproduce a continuación al pie de la letra.
sources.caption: Fuentes de datos del directorio español

es-regcess.use: Centros sanitarios: nombres, tipos, oferta asistencial, titularidad pública o privada, direcciones, municipios, teléfonos
es-regcess.frequency: Cada mes, por el Ministerio de Sanidad

es-ign.use: Comunidades autónomas, provincias y municipios, y el núcleo principal de cada municipio, donde se sitúan sus centros

map.name: Datos cartográficos
map.publisher: Colaboradores de OpenStreetMap, teselas de OpenFreeMap

sources.conditions: El registro se muestra tal como se publica: nombres en minúsculas con mayúscula inicial, solo los datos propios del centro, sin alterar nunca su sentido. Cada página española cita la fuente y la fecha de su última actualización.
sources.legalNotice: Aviso legal del Ministerio de Sanidad

coverage.heading: Centros incluidos
body: Se generan páginas para los tipos de centro sanitario que visitan los pacientes, según el tipo de centro del registro. Una consulta médica o de otro profesional sanitario figura en el listado de su unidad asistencial principal; sus demás unidades se muestran en su página.

Quedan fuera: los demás centros con internamiento, los centros móviles, los centros de diagnóstico, de diálisis, de reproducción humana asistida, de cirugía mayor ambulatoria y de transfusión, los bancos de tejidos, los centros de salud mental, los centros de reconocimiento, los demás centros especializados y proveedores, los servicios dentro de un centro y los establecimientos distintos de las farmacias (botiquines, ópticas, ortopedias y establecimientos de audioprótesis).
El registro no publica coordenadas: cada centro se sitúa en el núcleo principal de su municipio (IGN). Su posición en el mapa y su distancia son las del municipio, nunca las de su dirección.

kinds.ES_MEDICAL_PRACTICE: Consultas médicas, por unidad asistencial principal (C21)
kinds.ES_OTHER_PRACTICE: Consultas de otros profesionales sanitarios, por unidad asistencial principal (C22)

identifiers.heading: Identificadores
body: La dirección de cada página termina con el código de centro normalizado (CCN) que el registro asigna al centro, para que una página pueda encontrarse y contrastarse con el registro:
list: /es/centro/clinica-dental-ejemplo-centro-1328900001: el código de centro 1328900001.
No se usan el código autonómico del centro ni el NIF de su titular.

correct.heading: Corregir un error
body: Las páginas reproducen el registro: la corrección duradera se hace en la fuente, y la página se actualiza en la siguiente importación tras la publicación mensual del registro.
Para cualquier otra cosa, use el formulario: revisamos cada notificación.
list: Nombre, dirección, tipo de centro, oferta asistencial: el titular del centro lo comunica a la consejería de sanidad de su comunidad autónoma, que autorizó el centro e inscribe el cambio en el registro.
Número de teléfono: del mismo modo, ante la consejería de sanidad de la comunidad autónoma.
correct.formBody: Indique la dirección de la página y qué es incorrecto.

remove.heading: Retirar una página
body: Cualquier persona a la que se refiera una página puede oponerse a su publicación en cualquier momento, sin dar motivos (artículo 21 del RGPD). Una página no reclamada se oculta en cuanto llega la solicitud y se elimina tras una comprobación sencilla; no vuelve con las actualizaciones del registro. Una página reclamada la retira su titular, desde su espacio.
remove.formTitle: Solicitar la retirada de una página
remove.formBody: Indique la dirección de la página y una dirección de correo electrónico en la que podamos responderle.

LegalNoticeCh.metaDescription: Impressum of the Swiss pages of Apercura: the provider, its contact address including e-mail, its registration and VAT number, and the person responsible for the content (Federal Act against Unfair Competition, UWG, article 3(1)(s)).
LegalNoticeCh.title: Impressum
LegalNoticeCh.lead: Who provides the Swiss pages of Apercura (apercura.org/ch, /ch-fr and /ch-it): the identity and the contact address, e-mail included, that article 3(1)(s) of the Federal Act against Unfair Competition (UWG) asks of anyone offering services online, as Swiss practice gives them in an Impressum.

provider.heading: Provider
body: The Swiss pages of Apercura are provided by the entity below. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of the hospitals and clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies of Switzerland, built from the open data of the Federal Office of Public Health and of the cantons, without advertising, with a space where a facility can complete its own page. Pages are facilities, never individual health professionals. No appointment is booked through Apercura in Switzerland.

editor.heading: Person responsible for the content
body: The person below is responsible for what the provider publishes. Information a facility adds to its own page is the facility’s own responsibility.

liability.heading: Content of the pages
body: The directory is built from the Federal Office of Public Health’s hospital figures for 2023 and from the lists of hospitals, nursing homes and pharmacies that cantons publish as open data, placed with the Federal Statistical Office’s commune register and swisstopo’s directory of localities. It can be incomplete or out of date: check the information with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The data is reused under the terms of use of opendata.swiss and of each publisher, with the attribution each one asks for: the data page lists every source.

review.heading: Status of this text
body: This text is a draft, written before the legal entity was set up. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Switzerland before the Swiss pages are announced.

PrivacyCh.metaDescription: Data processed by the Swiss pages of Apercura: sources, purposes, principles and grounds, disclosure abroad, retention, recipients and your rights, including objection (revised Federal Act on Data Protection, nFADP, and the GDPR).
PrivacyCh.title: Privacy
PrivacyCh.lead: What data the Swiss pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP), in force since 1 September 2023, and its ordinance (DSV).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the Impressum is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site. Write to the address below with any question about your data.

law.heading: Which law applies
body: The processing of the Swiss pages is subject to the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP, SR 235.1) and to the Data Protection Ordinance (DSV, SR 235.11). As the provider is established in the European Union, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) applies to its processing as well: a section below says what it adds.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the facility’s name as its list publishes it; its kind (hospital or clinic site, nursing home, pharmacy); for a hospital or clinic, its type in the Federal Statistical Office’s typology, its activity types, its emergency department and intensive care unit, its outpatient and inpatient offer, the legal form group of its hospital and its operator; the category its canton’s list gives it; its address, postcode, locality, commune and canton; its phone number where its list gives one, and its position where its list gives coordinates. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.
This is data about organisations. The nFADP protects data about natural persons only: a facility’s data is personal data where its name designates a person, as the next section explains.
Purpose: letting the public find a hospital, a clinic, a nursing home or a pharmacy, where it is and what it is.
Retention: as long as the facility appears in its list. A page disappears after two imports in which the facility is no longer in it; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they name
body: A Swiss page is a facility, never a person’s profile. No health professional is listed: no register of individual doctors, pharmacists or other professionals is imported.

A facility’s name can designate a person, for example a pharmacy named after its pharmacist (“Apotheke Dr. Muster”): that name is then personal data, taken from a list the Confederation or a canton publishes. A page prints the name as its list publishes it, without a care-of address and what follows it, which can name someone else. Nothing else about a person is collected: the names of responsible pharmacists, the e-mail addresses and the user names of the lists’ editors are never read, and there is no date of birth, no home address, no rating and no review.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from open government data: the Federal Office of Public Health’s (FOPH) “Kennzahlen der Schweizer Spitäler 2023”, the lists of hospitals, nursing homes and pharmacies that the cantons of Zürich, Bern, Geneva, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and Jura publish on opendata.swiss, the Federal Statistical Office’s official commune register and swisstopo’s official directory of localities with their postcodes. Each source is reused with the attribution it asks for:

grounds.heading: Principles and grounds
body: Under the nFADP, a private person may process personal data without consent as long as the processing follows the principles of articles 6 and 8 (lawfulness, good faith, proportionality, a recognisable and limited purpose, accuracy, data security) and the person concerned has not expressly objected to it (article 30(2)). Consent is not the general ground of processing, and the directory asks for none.

Where a page names a person, the provider relies on an overriding interest (article 31(1)): the public needs to know which hospitals, clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies are where, a need the Confederation and the cantons already meet by publishing these lists as open data. Only the facility’s own data is shown, in a neutral order, without advertising, ratings or reviews; an objection hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back.
Facility accounts and claims rest on the terms of use, a contract with the account holder (article 31(2)(a)), and on the provider’s interest in securing the service.

information.heading: How you are informed
body: The facility data does not come from the facilities themselves. For data not collected from the person concerned, article 19 of the nFADP asks the controller to give also the categories of data processed (paragraph 3), at the latest one month after obtaining them (paragraph 5).

This notice gives that information: the controller and its contact details, the purposes, the categories of data, the sources, the recipients, the disclosure abroad and your rights. It is linked from every page, and the data page lists each source. The people a facility’s name may designate are not known to the provider one by one: informing each of them individually would require a disproportionate effort (article 20(2)(b)).

objection.heading: Objecting to a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (nFADP articles 30(2)(b) and 32(2); GDPR article 21). If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough, on the data page or on the page itself: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the lists never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: e-mail address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Grounds: the terms of use (nFADP article 31(2)(a); GDPR article 6(1)(b)) and the interest in securing the service (GDPR article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact e-mail address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is my page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.

Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Grounds: the interest in an accurate directory and the right to object (nFADP articles 31(1) and 32(2); GDPR articles 6(1)(f) and 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, kind and identifier shown in their space and their claim, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data, cookies and local storage
body: Only what the service technically needs is stored in your browser: the session cookie of signed-in facilities and, in the browser’s local storage, the light or dark display you chose, which is never sent to the server. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

Article 45c of the Telecommunications Act (TCA) asks that you be told what is stored on your device and why, and that you can refuse it: you can block or delete these items in your browser’s settings, signing in then no longer works.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, bound by contract to process it only as the provider instructs and to keep it secure (nFADP article 9; GDPR article 28). Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

abroad.heading: Disclosure abroad
body: Data may be processed in states of the European Economic Area, whose legislation the Federal Council recognises as providing adequate protection (nFADP article 16(1) and annex 1 of the DSV): no other safeguard is needed. Nothing is disclosed elsewhere; any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated individual decisions
body: No decision about you is based exclusively on automated processing (nFADP article 21). A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask whether data about you is processed and receive it (right of access, nFADP article 25), receive the data you provided in a common electronic format or have it transmitted to another controller (article 28), have inaccurate data corrected, and have data erased or its processing or disclosure stopped (article 32). Write to the address below; access is given free of charge, within 30 days.

You can also report a processing you consider contrary to data protection rules to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC), Feldeggweg 1, 3003 Bern, www.edoeb.admin.ch, who can open an investigation (article 49).

gdpr.heading: Visitors in the European Union and the EEA
body: The GDPR applies to the provider’s processing as well, in particular for visitors in the European Union and the European Economic Area. This notice gives the information its articles 13 and 14 require; the facility data is processed on the ground of legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)), weighed as above. You can object at any time to the processing of data about you (article 21), ask for its processing to be restricted (article 18), and lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority of the state where you live or work (article 77). Requests go to the same address and are answered within one month.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Switzerland and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

TermsCh.metaDescription: Terms of use of the Swiss pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of hospitals and clinics, nursing homes and pharmacies from the open data of the Federal Office of Public Health and the cantons, without online booking.
TermsCh.title: Terms of use
TermsCh.lead: The rules for using the Swiss pages of Apercura, for the public and for facilities alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the hospital and clinic sites, nursing homes and pharmacies of the open lists the Federal Office of Public Health and the cantons publish. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Switzerland. It is run by the provider named in the Impressum.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from the public lists, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement.
The information may be incomplete or out of date: check it with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice

practices.heading: For facilities
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it, checked by an administrator before the page is handed over.
The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to it and ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder. Errors in the data are corrected at the source, with the canton or the federal office that publishes the list, or reported with the form of the data page.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information facilities add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: The governing law and the competent courts will be specified during the legal review; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

scope.heading: Scope

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The FOPH’s hospital figures are a yearly edition, and the directory reads the 2023 one; the cantons update their lists at their own pace. The directory checks the lists every month and imports a list when it has changed. A page changes only when its facts change in its list.

Each attribution below is printed word for word, in this page’s language where the publisher words it in that language; the attribution of Geneva’s lists names the day they were downloaded, the day of the last Swiss import.

sources.conditions: The lists are shown as published, without changing their meaning: a facility’s name as its list writes it, without a care-of address and what follows it, and the facility’s own data only. Every Swiss page cites the lists it is built from, with their attributions.
sources.termsText: The terms of use of opendata.swiss

coverage.heading: Facilities covered
body: A page is a facility, never a person. What is listed depends on what each canton publishes as open data:
coverage.elsewhere: Elsewhere, no nursing home or pharmacy is listed yet, and no medical or dental practice is listed anywhere.

kinds.CH_HOSPITAL: General hospitals: university hospitals, centre care and basic care (FSO types K111 to K123)
kinds.CH_SPECIALTY_CLINIC: Specialised clinics: surgery, gynaecology and neonatology, paediatrics, geriatrics and others (K231 to K235)
kinds.CH_NURSING_HOME: Nursing homes, where a canton lists them
kinds.CH_PHARMACY: Pharmacies, where a canton lists them

excluded.heading: What is not imported, and why
body: Some data would complete the directory but cannot be reused, or is not needed:
list: Health professionals: the federal registers of the medical professions (MedReg), the psychology professions (PsyReg) and the health professions (GesReg) can be consulted one entry at a time; their bulk data needs an agreement with the FOPH, which the directory does not have. No person is listed.
Refdata’s partner data (GLN numbers of professionals and businesses): not open data; republishing it needs Refdata’s written consent.
OpenStreetMap: used for the base map only, never as a source of facilities or of their positions, since its Open Database Licence (ODbL) is share-alike.
The FOPH’s hospital figures for 2024: their terms ask for permission before any commercial use, so the 2023 edition, open with the source, is read.
Data about individuals, never: no register of people, no ratings, no reviews.

unread.heading: Fields never read
body: The lists hold some fields a page does not need, some of which name or reach a person. They are never read or stored:
list: The name of the responsible pharmacist in the canton of Basel-Landschaft’s list of pharmacies.
E-mail addresses, in every list.
The user name of the editor of each record in the canton of Jura’s file.
The figures of the FOPH’s workbook (costs, staff, cases): a page needs none of them.
A care-of or attention mention in a facility’s name, and what follows it.

locations.heading: Locations
body: Every facility is placed in its canton, district and commune, from the Federal Statistical Office’s official commune register: by the commune number where its list gives one, else by its postcode and locality, from swisstopo’s official directory of localities.

Its point is the one its list gives, converted from the Swiss national grid where needed. The FOPH’s figures and some lists give no coordinates: such a facility is shown at the point of its locality in swisstopo’s directory. No pin marks it on a map, and its distance is approximate.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: Switzerland publishes no open national number of a health facility: the address of every page ends with the key of its list, after letters naming that list, so that a page can be found and checked against its source:
list: /ch/einrichtung/spital-beispiel-h123456789: a site of the FOPH’s figures, which give it no number; its key is derived from its canton, hospital, name and postcode, after h.
/ch/einrichtung/apotheke-beispiel-blp7601000000000: the Global Location Number (GLN) of a pharmacy in the canton of Basel-Landschaft’s list, after blp.

/ch/einrichtung/pflegeheim-beispiel-gee123456: the cantonal address identifier (IDPADR) of a nursing home in Geneva’s list, after gee; the identifier of a home in the canton of Zürich’s list follows zhe.
The other lists number no facility: their key is derived from the facility’s name and address, after letters naming the canton and the list (beh, bee, geh, gep, ble, bsh, bse, ju).

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the public lists: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the corrected list is published.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A facility from a canton’s list: ask the cantonal office that publishes the list, named in the sources above, to correct it.
A hospital or clinic site from the FOPH’s figures: the 2023 figures are not published again; report the error with the form below.
Phone, website and opening hours: where the list gives none, a facility adds them by claiming its page.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (nFADP articles 30(2)(b) and 32(2); GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the updates of the lists. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form.
remove.formTitle: Ask for a page to be removed
remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an e-mail address where we can answer you.

provider.heading: Service provider
body: The Slovenian pages of Apercura are operated by the entity below. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of the doctors who can be chosen as a personal doctor in Slovenia (family doctors, children’s and school doctors, gynaecologists and dentists), built from the open data of the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia (ZZZS), without advertising, with a space where a doctor can complete their own page. No appointment is booked through Apercura in Slovenia.

Information a doctor adds to their own page is their own responsibility; as a service that stores information provided by its users, the operator answers for it only under the conditions of the ZEPT and of article 6 of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065).

liability.heading: Content of the pages
body: The directory is built from the lists of the doctors who can be personal doctors, which the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia (ZZZS) publishes every day as open data under CC BY 4.0. The providers report their doctors’ data to ZZZS and answer for its accuracy; it can be incomplete or out of date: check with the practice before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The directory data is reused under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0): the data page lists every source with the attribution it requires.
