PrivacyIe.metaDescription: Data processed by the Irish pages of Apercura: sources, purposes, legal bases, retention, recipients and your rights, including objection (GDPR articles 13, 14 and 21, Data Protection Act 2018).
PrivacyIe.title: Privacy notice
PrivacyIe.lead: What data the Irish pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The service provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of facility accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about facilities
body: Data: the facility's name as its register publishes it, its kind (pharmacy, nursing home, hospital, health centre), its address and Eircode, its town and county, its telephone number where the list gives one, for a hospital its kind as the HSE names it, for a nursing home its number of places for residents and the link to its page on HIQA's website, and who runs it when that is the HSE or a company. A facility that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.

Identifier: the PSI's registration number of the pharmacy, HIQA's centre number of the nursing home, or a key derived from a hospital's or health centre's county, name and address, at the end of the page's address.
Purpose: letting the public find a pharmacy, a nursing home, a hospital or a health centre, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.

Retention: as long as the facility is on its register or list. A page disappears at the import after the facility has left it (a pharmacy struck off the register, for example); a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the facilities themselves (GDPR article 14). This notice gives the information article 14 asks for, on the site where the pages are: the categories of data, their sources, the purposes and legal basis, the retention, the recipients and your rights, including the right to object. Every page links to it, and the data page lists the sources.

people.heading: Facilities, and the people they may name
body: An Irish page is a facility, never a person's profile. No register of individual doctors, nurses, pharmacists or other clinicians is imported, and the HSE's layer of GP practices, which names doctors, is not read.

A facility's details can still be about a person in three cases. A pharmacy's trading name may be a person's name (“Example's Pharmacy”): it is shown as the PSI's register publishes it, since another name would mislead. A nursing home's operator is shown only when it is the HSE or a company registered with the Companies Registration Office whose name names no person; an individual provider or a partnership is never stored. A facility's phone is its own line, but one that reaches a sole trader directly can be personal data.

Never read or stored, although the lists publish them: the owner of a pharmacy business, its superintendent and supervising pharmacists, a nursing home's person in charge and their phone, management contacts, the provider's own address and phone, and every email address. No rating and no review is collected.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Every page is built from a public register or open government data, re-used with the attribution each publisher asks for. The PSI must publish its registers on the Internet, free of charge (Pharmacy Act 2007, section 13); HIQA's registers of designated centres are open to inspection by the public and made available on the Internet (Health Act 2007, section 49(3)):

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: people need to know where the registered pharmacies, nursing homes, hospitals and health centres are and how to reach them, the need for which the law has the PSI and HIQA publish their registers on the Internet.

Necessity: only what identifies and reaches a facility is shown, as its register publishes it: its name, kind, address and phone. A pharmacy registered under a person's name cannot be listed under another without misleading; everything else that names a person is left out.

Balance: the same facts are on the public register and, for a pharmacy, on its shop front, so a facility listed by its regulator expects to be found in a directory repeating them. No special category of data, no rating, no review, no comparison, no paid placement; a neutral order; an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back; corrections at the source; pages that follow every import of the registers. Weighing these points, the interests of the public prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Facility accounts and claims
body: Data: email address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right facility. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact email address when one is given and the page concerned; for an “I run this facility” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping a facility that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again. A holder who removes their page keeps, in their account only and never published, the name, kind and identifier shown in their space, their claim and the places their agenda uses, until the account is deleted.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in facilities and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; facility sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page's holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: The directory's pages are public. Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider's team and the processors below receive the other data, each for its own part. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor's IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
body: The data is hosted and processed in the European Economic Area. Nothing is transferred outside it; any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Commission, Ireland's supervisory authority (GDPR article 77; Data Protection Act 2018, section 11): 6 Pembroke Row, Dublin 2, D02 X963, www.dataprotection.ie. The provider is established in France, so its lead supervisory authority is the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), with which you can lodge a complaint too: www.cnil.fr.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the imports of the registers never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

changes.heading: Updates to this notice
body: This notice is a draft. It will be reviewed by a lawyer qualified in Ireland and by the data protection officer; every version is dated.

TermsIe.metaDescription: Terms of use of the Irish pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of pharmacies, nursing homes, hospitals and health centres, without online booking.
TermsIe.title: Terms of use
TermsIe.lead: The rules for using the Irish pages of Apercura, for the public and for facilities alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the pharmacies on the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland's register, the nursing homes on HIQA's register of designated centres for older people, and the hospitals and health centres of the HSE's Health Atlas. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Ireland. It is run by the service provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from public registers and lists, as they publish it, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement. No facility pays to be listed or to be shown first, and none is endorsed. They list facilities, never individual clinicians.

Each list has its own date: the PSI's register as of the date it gives, HIQA's register as of the last import, the HSE's hospitals and health centres as recorded in March 2020. The information may be incomplete or out of date: check it with the facility before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112 or 999. Outside your GP's hours, contact the GP out-of-hours service for your area; a pharmacist can advise on minor illnesses.

facilities.heading: For facilities
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.
The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, and must not advertise a product or service.

removal.heading: Correcting or removing a page
body: A fact taken from a register is corrected with the body that publishes it, and the page follows at the next import; anything else can be reported with the form on the data page. Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information facilities add to their pages. Nothing in these terms limits a liability that the law does not allow to be limited, such as liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence. These terms will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. Directory data is re-used under the re-use conditions of the PSI and HIQA and under CC BY 4.0: the data page lists every source.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by French law, the law of the provider's establishment. If you use the site as a consumer living in Ireland, you keep the protection of the mandatory rules of Irish law and can bring a claim before the Irish courts. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityIe.metaDescription: Accessibility of the Irish pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityIe.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityIe.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Irish pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: This statement is voluntary. The European Union (Accessibility of Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Sector Bodies) Regulations 2020 (S.I. No. 358 of 2020) bind public sector bodies, which Apercura is not, and the European Union (Accessibility Requirements of Products and Services) Regulations 2023 (S.I. No. 636 of 2023) bind the services they list, among them e-commerce services, which a free directory is not. Its provider nevertheless aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Irish pages share the code of the other markets' pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress. The pages are in English only for now.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

DataIe.metaDescription: Where the Irish pages of Apercura come from: the PSI's register of pharmacies, HIQA's register of nursing homes, the HSE's Health Atlas layers and the places of Tailte Éireann and the CSO, with their terms, dates, what is not imported, and how to correct or remove a page.
DataIe.title: Data and sources
DataIe.lead: Every Irish page is built from a public register or open government data. Here is where it comes from, under which terms and attribution, how old each list is, what is left out and why, and how to correct or remove a page.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The PSI publishes its register of pharmacies every month, and HIQA's register of nursing homes is exported as it stands on the day of each import. The directory imports a list when it has changed; a page changes only when its facts change in its list.
status.notImported: The Irish directory has not been imported yet on this site.

dates.heading: How old each list is
body: Each list is as old as its publisher's last edition, and the HSE's is old: its Health Atlas gave its layers of hospitals and health centres to GeoHive in March 2020, and no more recent open list of the HSE's facilities was found. The HSE's 2017 list on data.ehealthireland.ie is older still and can no longer be downloaded; the CSO's 2026 “Distance to Services” layers give distances to services, not a list of facilities. A hospital or health centre opened, renamed or closed since March 2020 is therefore missing or out of date here: its page says so.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: The PSI's and HIQA's registers are re-used under their publishers' re-use conditions; the HSE's layers and the places of Tailte Éireann and the CSO are published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), which asks for the source to be credited. Each attribution below is printed word for word, and every Irish page prints those of its own sources.
sources.caption: Data sources of the Irish directory

ie-psi.use: Retail pharmacy businesses: names as registered, addresses, Eircodes, towns and counties, registration numbers

ie-hiqa.use: Designated centres for older people (nursing homes): names, addresses, Eircodes, counties, phone numbers, places for residents, the operator when it is the HSE or a company, the link to the centre's inspection reports
ie-hiqa.frequency: Exported from HIQA's register at each import

ie-hse-hospitals.use: Public, voluntary and private hospitals: names, addresses, kinds of hospital, points

ie-hse-health-centres.use: The HSE's health centres: names, addresses, points

ie-counties.use: The 26 counties, in which every facility is placed

ie-towns.use: The towns of the 2022 census (Built Up Areas), in which facilities are placed, and the point of each town

ie-placenames.use: The names of towns and villages, to match the town a list writes with the census's

map.name: Map data
map.use: The base map of the pages

conditions: The PSI's terms of use allow free re-use of its registers in any format, provided the source and its copyright are acknowledged, the information is reproduced accurately and not used in a misleading way, and the user agrees to “Not use the information for the principal purpose of advertising or promoting a particular product or service”. They refer to the latest PSI licence on data.gov.ie, today the Open Data Licence of data.gov.ie (CC BY 4.0), which does not cover personal data. HIQA's re-use conditions point to the same PSI licence.

Apercura's use fits these conditions: it is a free directory without advertising, which lists every registered pharmacy and nursing home the same way, in a neutral order, sells no placement or ranking, promotes no product or service, and links each page to the register it comes from. The rules on advertising that bind pharmacists (the PSI's guidance and code of conduct) and on advertising medicinal products (S.I. No. 541 of 2007) concern what a pharmacy or a supplier publishes: Apercura names no medicine, and no listing is paid for or endorsed.

coverage.heading: Facilities covered
body: A page is a facility, never a person. Ireland's pages list:

kinds.IE_PHARMACY: Pharmacies: every retail pharmacy business on the PSI's register
kinds.IE_NURSING_HOME: Nursing homes: every designated centre for older people on HIQA's register
kinds.IE_HOSPITAL: Hospitals: the public, voluntary and private hospitals of the HSE's Health Atlas, March 2020
kinds.IE_HEALTH_CENTRE: Health centres: the HSE's health centres of the Health Atlas, March 2020

excluded.heading: What is not imported, and why
body: Some data would complete the directory but cannot be re-used, or is not needed:
list: GP practices: the HSE's layer of GP practices names the doctors, so it is not read. No GP, dentist or other clinic is listed.

Health professionals: the registers of doctors (Medical Council), nurses and midwives (NMBI), dentists (Dental Council) and pharmacists (PSI) can be searched one entry at a time, but are not published for re-use. No person is listed.
HIQA's register of designated centres for people with disabilities: it gives no address of its centres.
OpenStreetMap: used for the base map only, never as a source of facilities or of their positions, since its Open Database Licence (ODbL) is share-alike.
Data about individuals, never: no register of people, no ratings, no reviews.

unread.heading: Fields never read
body: The lists hold some fields a page does not need, some of which name or reach a person. They are never read or stored:
list: The owner of a pharmacy business and its superintendent and supervising pharmacists, in the PSI's register.

A nursing home's person in charge and their phone, its management contacts, and the provider's own address and phone, in HIQA's register; the provider's name only when it is the HSE or a company whose name names no person.
Email addresses, in every list.

locations.heading: Locations
body: Every facility is placed in its county, from Tailte Éireann's boundaries, and in its town, from the CSO's Built Up Areas of the 2022 census, by the town and county its list writes. A facility whose town is not one of the census's is placed in its county only: it appears in its county's listing.

Eircodes are printed as part of an address, as the lists publish them, but never used to locate a facility: the Eircode database is not open data. A pharmacy or a nursing home is shown at the point of its town: no pin marks it on a map, and its distance is approximate. A hospital or health centre is shown at the point the HSE's layer gives it, as recorded in March 2020.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: The address of every page ends with a key, after a letter naming its list, so that a page can be found and checked against its source:
list: /ie/facility/example-pharmacy-p1234: the PSI's registration number of a pharmacy, after p.
/ie/facility/example-nursing-home-n738: HIQA's centre number of a nursing home, after n.
/ie/facility/example-hospital-h123456789: the HSE's layer numbers no hospital, so its key is derived from its county, name and address, after h; a health centre's follows c.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the public registers: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import after the corrected list is published.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A pharmacy: the pharmacy business tells the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland, which keeps its register.
A nursing home: the registered provider tells HIQA, which keeps the register of designated centres.
A hospital or health centre: the HSE's March 2020 layers are not published again; report the error with the form below.
Phone, website and opening hours: where the list gives none, a facility adds them by claiming its page.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the imports of the registers. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space. Every page also has its own removal form.
remove.formTitle: Ask for a page to be removed
remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an email address where we can answer you.

LegalNoticeFi.metaDescription: Legal notice of the Finnish pages of Apercura: the service provider, its business id, address and contact details, e-mail included (Act 917/2014, section 176).
LegalNoticeFi.title: Legal notice
LegalNoticeFi.lead: Who provides the Finnish pages of Apercura (apercura.org/fi): the information that section 176 of the Act on Electronic Communications Services (laki sähköisen viestinnän palveluista, 917/2014) asks a service provider to keep easily, directly and permanently available.

provider.heading: Service provider (Act 917/2014, section 176)
body: The Finnish pages of Apercura are provided by the entity below: its name, its address, its contact details, e-mail included, the trade register or other public register that keeps it with its registration number or business id, and its VAT number when it is registered for VAT. It runs the directory and answers for its content.

service.heading: The service
body: A free directory of the public health service locations of Finland (health centres, hospitals, emergency clinics, dental clinics, maternity and child health clinics, mental health and substance abuse services, rehabilitation units, laboratories and imaging), built from the national Finnish Service Catalogue (Suomi.fi-palvelutietovaranto, PTV), where the wellbeing services counties, the City of Helsinki, Åland and the other public organisers describe them, without advertising, with a space where an organiser can complete its own pages. Pages are places, never the health workers who work there. Pharmacies and private clinics are not listed. The pages are in Finnish; Swedish, Finland’s other national language, is planned.

booking.heading: No booking in Finland
body: No appointment is booked through Apercura in Finland. An appointment system for health care processes client data under the Act on the Processing of Client Data in Healthcare and Social Welfare (784/2021): such systems are registered as class A or B and connected to the national Kanta services. Whether a booking tool used alongside them must itself be registered and connected to Kanta has not been settled; until it is, Apercura only publishes a directory, which processes no client data. To make an appointment, contact the service location or its organiser.

editor.heading: Responsible for the content
body: The person below is responsible for what the provider publishes. Information an organiser adds to its own page is its own responsibility; as a host of information provided by its users, the provider answers for it only under the conditions of the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, article 6).

liability.heading: Content of the pages
body: The directory is built from the Finnish Service Catalogue, whose content each organiser keeps up to date, and placed in Statistics Finland’s municipalities, wellbeing services counties and regions. It can be incomplete or out of date: check opening hours and how to get care with the service location or its organiser before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

advertising.heading: Factual information, no advertising
body: Marketing of health services in Finland must be factual and must not mislead (Consumer Protection Act 38/1978, chapter 2; the professional bodies’ guidelines, such as the Finnish Medical Association’s, add their own rules). The former marketing provision of the Private Health Care Act (152/1990) was repealed, with that act, by the Act on the Supervision of Social and Health Care (741/2023) from 1 January 2024.

Apercura is paid by no one for a page. It publishes the same facts, from the national catalogue, for every service location and in the same form: name, kind, organiser, services, address, telephone. No ranking, no rating, no review, no paid placement, no promotional wording; listings follow a neutral order. An organiser that claims its page may add factual information only, under the same rule.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code of Apercura is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The Finnish Service Catalogue’s data is reused under CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication); Statistics Finland’s municipalities, wellbeing services counties and regions under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0), with its credit. The data page lists every source with the credit it requires.

review.heading: Status of this text
body: This text is a draft, written before the legal entity was set up. It will be reviewed by a lawyer admitted in Finland before the Finnish pages are announced.

PrivacyFi.lead: What data the Finnish pages of Apercura process, where it comes from, why, for how long and by whom, and how to exercise your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Data Protection Act (tietosuojalaki, 1050/2018).

controller.heading: Who is responsible
body: The provider named in the legal notice is the controller of the directory, of organiser accounts, of claims and of the requests sent through the site.

directory.heading: Directory: data about public service locations
body: Data: the name of the service location as the Finnish Service Catalogue publishes it, its kind, the services the catalogue links to it, the organisation that describes it (its organiser), its street address, postcode, post office and municipality, its point on the map and the first public telephone number the catalogue gives for it (often the organiser’s booking or advice line, shared by several of its locations). An organiser that claims its page can add a presentation, languages, a photo and opening hours.
Never stored, although the catalogue publishes them: e-mail addresses, the catalogue’s free-text descriptions and service hours.
Identifier: a page ends with the catalogue’s permanent id of the service location, without its dashes (for example b18aa7f87eca4b97a8e8b438d2e29427).
Purpose: letting the public find a public health service location, what it offers, where it is and how to reach it. Legal basis: legitimate interests (GDPR article 6(1)(f)), assessed below.
Retention: as long as the location appears in the catalogue. A page disappears when the catalogue no longer lists it; a page removed after an objection is never published again.

Information: the data does not come from the organisers themselves (GDPR article 14). Writing to each of them would involve a disproportionate effort (article 14(5)(b)); this notice, the data page and a notice on every page make the information public.

people.heading: Places, not people
body: A Finnish page is a public service location, never a person’s profile: the catalogue’s service location records name no health worker, and no health worker is listed. Should a location’s name contain a person’s name (a unit named after its founder, for example), the page shows it as the catalogue publishes it, as part of the name of a public place; the categories of data concerned are those listed above; their source is the Finnish Service Catalogue; their recipient is the public.
Nothing else about any person is collected: no personal identity code, no private address, no e-mail, no ratings and no reviews. No patient’s data, and no health data, is processed by the directory.
Anyone a page is about can object to it at any time, and the page is removed.

sources.heading: Sources
body: Service locations come from the Finnish Service Catalogue (Suomi.fi-palvelutietovaranto), run by the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (Digi- ja väestötietovirasto, DVV), whose content the public organisers describe and which is published through its open interface under CC0 1.0. Municipalities, wellbeing services counties and regions come from Statistics Finland (CC BY 4.0). Each source is credited as it asks:

balancing.heading: Legitimate interests assessment
body: Purpose: patients need to know which public health services exist where, what they offer and how to reach them, a need the State already meets by publishing the national catalogue for everyone to reuse.

Necessity: only the catalogue’s data about places is shown, data the catalogue publishes anyway, and less of it: no e-mail, no free-text description; nothing about private life, no ratings, no reviews.

Balance: a public service context, factual information, a neutral order, no advertising, the minimum of the catalogue’s fields, an objection that hides a page at once and keeps it from coming back, corrections at the source, and pages that follow every update of the catalogue. Weighing these points, the interests of patients prevail, and anyone a page is about can object without giving a reason.

accounts.heading: Organiser accounts and claims
body: Data: e-mail address, name, password (stored hashed), second authentication factor, the documents sent to claim a page (proof that the claimant acts for the organiser of the service location) and team members.

Purposes: managing the account and checking that a page is claimed by the right organiser. Legal bases: performance of the terms of use (article 6(1)(b)) and the legitimate interests of securing the service (article 6(1)(f)).
Retention: the account is kept until it is deleted; supporting documents, encrypted, are erased 30 days after the decision.

requests.heading: Error reports, objections and contact requests
body: Data: the message, the contact e-mail address when one is given and the page concerned; for a “this is our page” request also the name and phone number. Free text is encrypted.
Purposes: correcting errors, applying objections and helping an organiser that cannot claim its page online. Legal bases: legitimate interests (article 6(1)(f)) and the right to object (article 21).

Retention: a report is deleted 6 months after it is closed, a rejected objection one year after its decision, a contact request 12 months after the last exchange. Once an objection is confirmed, or the holder of a claimed page removes it, the page and the data about it are deleted at once, the objection included; all that is kept is a record of the removal (the identifier of the page, the country, the reason, who recorded it and when), so that it is never published again.

technical.heading: Technical data and cookies
body: Only cookies strictly necessary to the service are set: the session of signed-in organisers and the chosen language. No advertising or audience measurement cookies, no trackers.

To limit abuse, IP addresses are transformed with a keyed function before being counted and never stored as such; organiser sessions record a truncated IP address. Views of claimed pages are counted without a cookie or identifier, and only the page’s holder sees them.

recipients.heading: Recipients and processors
body: Data is neither sold nor rented, and never used for advertising. Only the provider’s team and the processors below receive it, each for its own part, under a contract that meets GDPR article 28. The data is hosted in the European Economic Area. Maps are loaded from a tile server, which receives the visitor’s IP address like any website.

transfers.heading: Transfers outside the European Union
body: Data is transferred outside the European Union and the European Economic Area only under the safeguards of chapter V of the GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses). Any change of processor will be announced here before it takes effect.

automated.heading: Automated decisions
body: No decision about you is taken by automated means alone. A claim is decided by a person, who reads its documents.

rights.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing, to receive it in a portable format and to object to its processing. Write to the address below; you will get an answer within one month.

You can also lodge a complaint with the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman (Tietosuojavaltuutetun toimisto), Finland’s supervisory authority (GDPR article 77; Data Protection Act, section 8), or with the supervisory authority of the country where you live or work.

objection.heading: Objecting to a page (GDPR article 21)
body: Anyone a page is about can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason. If the page is unclaimed, a form is enough: the page is hidden as soon as the request arrives, deleted after a light check, and the updates of the catalogue never publish it again. If it is claimed, its holder removes it from their space.

TermsFi.metaDescription: Terms of use of the Finnish pages of Apercura: a free, factual directory of public health service locations from the Finnish Service Catalogue, without booking.
TermsFi.title: Terms of use
TermsFi.lead: The rules for using the Finnish pages of Apercura, for the public and for the organisers of the places listed alike.

service.heading: The service
body: Apercura lists, free of charge, the public health service locations that the wellbeing services counties, the City of Helsinki, Åland and the other public organisers describe in the Finnish Service Catalogue. It lists places, not the health workers who work there, and neither pharmacies nor private clinics. It is a directory only: no appointment is booked through Apercura in Finland, because whether a booking tool must be a registered system connected to Kanta (Act 784/2021) has not been settled. It is run by the provider named in the legal notice.
Using the directory requires no account. Using the site means accepting these terms.

content.heading: What the pages contain
body: Pages show factual information from the Finnish Service Catalogue, as it publishes it, in a neutral order, without ratings, reviews, advertising or paid placement.

The information may be incomplete or out of date, and a location without a point in the catalogue is shown at its municipality, not at its exact address on a map: check opening hours and how to get care with the location or its organiser before you go. Every page says how to report an error.

health.heading: Not medical advice
body: Apercura gives no medical advice and is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 112. The medical helpline (Päivystysapu) answers at 116 117.

providers.heading: For organisers
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant acts for the organiser of the service location, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date: marketing of health services must not mislead (Consumer Protection Act, chapter 2), and only facts such as the location’s name, opening hours, address, services, languages and prices may be published.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page is about can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information organisers add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The Finnish Service Catalogue’s data is in the public domain (CC0 1.0); Statistics Finland’s places are under CC BY 4.0: anyone may reuse them from these pages with the credit “Lähde: Tilastokeskus”.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by Finnish law; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. The competent court will be specified during the legal review. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution; a consumer can also turn to the Consumer Disputes Board (kuluttajariitalautakunta).

AccessibilityFi.metaDescription: Accessibility of the Finnish pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityFi.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityFi.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Finnish pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: The Act on the Provision of Digital Services (laki digitaalisten palvelujen tarjoamisesta, 306/2019) binds public bodies and the private services it lists, and the accessibility requirements act for products and services (102/2023) covers e-commerce and the other services it lists, not a free directory: their supervision does not apply to these pages. Apercura’s provider nevertheless publishes this statement in the form the act asks for and aims at the same standard on every page: WCAG 2.2 level AA (EN 301 549).
The pages are in Finnish. A Swedish version, in Finland’s other national language, is planned.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Finnish pages share the code of the other markets’ pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, in Finnish.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages, including the Finnish texts.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within two weeks and, where needed, give you the information in another form.

status.body: The organisers update their descriptions in the Finnish Service Catalogue whenever they change, and its open interface serves them at once; the directory reads the catalogue every week. A page changes only when its facts change in the catalogue.
status.notImported: The Finnish directory has not been imported yet on this site.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: The Digital and Population Data Services Agency publishes the Finnish Service Catalogue through its open interface under CC0 1.0, which asks for no credit: Apercura names it anyway. licence.heading: The licence of the Finnish data
body: The Finnish Service Catalogue’s content is free to use through its open interface, under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 public domain dedication, as its dataset on avoindata.fi states. Apercura makes no licence claim on it as republished on these pages: the AGPL-3.0 licence covers Apercura’s source code, not this data.
list: Statistics Finland’s municipalities, wellbeing services counties and regions are reused under CC BY 4.0, with the credit “Lähde: Tilastokeskus” and the year of the areas, on every page they place.

The catalogue’s version 11 interface, which needs no key, is read today; its version 12 asks for a free key registered by the user organisation, which Apercura will request before version 11 is switched off (announced for April 2027).
licence.changes: The catalogue is read every week and only what a page needs is kept: the service locations whose services are health care (health centres, hospitals, emergency clinics, dental clinics, maternity and child health clinics, mental health and substance abuse services, rehabilitation, laboratories and imaging); schools, libraries, social services and offices are left out, and so are school and student health care, e-mail addresses, free-text descriptions and service hours. coverage.heading: Places covered
body: Pages are generated for every service location of the Finnish Service Catalogue linked to a health care service, described by a public organiser: the 21 wellbeing services counties, the City of Helsinki, Åland, HUS and the other public bodies that describe their services there. A location is listed once, under the first kind its services give: a hospital, an emergency clinic, a health centre, a dental clinic, a maternity and child health clinic, a mental health or substance abuse service, a rehabilitation unit, then a laboratory or imaging unit. Every service is shown on the page.

Not listed: pharmacies (the Finnish Medicines Agency, Fimea, publishes no open-licensed list of pharmacies; its CC BY 4.0 open data covers medicines only), private clinics and practices (the register of private providers states no reuse licence), school and student health care, and the health workers, whom the catalogue does not name.

A location is placed at the catalogue’s point. A location without a point is placed at the centre of its municipality: its map position and its distance are then those of the municipality, never of the address.

providers.heading: For facilities
body: Claiming a page is free. It requires a document proving that the claimant runs the facility or acts for it, checked by a person before the page is handed over.

The holder of a page is responsible for the information they add. It must stay factual, accurate and up to date, and respect the rules on the advertising of health services, of medicines and of pharmacies; it must not name health professionals who have not agreed to it.

removal.heading: Removing a page
body: Anyone a page concerns can ask for it to be removed at any time: the data page explains how. A claimed page can only be removed by its holder.

liability.heading: Liability
body: The provider does its best to keep the service available and accurate, but cannot guarantee it. It is not responsible for the information facilities add to their pages. These limits will be specified during the legal review.

ip.heading: Code and data
body: The source code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence. The lists are reused under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0): anyone may reuse them, from data.gov.cy or from these pages, under that licence and with its credit.

law.heading: Governing law and disputes
body: The governing law will be specified during the legal review; the mandatory consumer protection rules of the country of residence always apply. In case of a dispute, first write to the contact address to look for an amicable solution.

AccessibilityCy.metaDescription: Accessibility of the Cypriot pages of Apercura: the WCAG 2.2 AA target, what was checked, what remains, and how to report a problem.
AccessibilityCy.title: Accessibility
AccessibilityCy.lead: Apercura is designed for everyone, including older and low-vision people. This statement says where the Cypriot pages stand.

scope.heading: Scope
body: Law 50(I)/2019 on the accessibility of the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies binds public bodies, and the accessibility requirements for products and services (Directive (EU) 2019/882) cover e-commerce and the other services they list, not a free directory: this statement is voluntary. Apercura’s provider aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA (EN 301 549) on every page.

status.heading: Where the site stands
body: The Cypriot pages share the code of the other markets’ pages and their tests. The site partially meets WCAG 2.2 AA: this rests on a self-assessment and automated tests, not yet on a full audit, which is in progress.

tests.heading: What was checked
list: Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules, levels A and AA) on every page type, at every release.
Keyboard-only journeys with a visible focus.
Body text of at least 18 px, targets of at least 44 px, nothing that relies on colour alone, no horizontal scrolling at 390 px.

pending.heading: What remains to be checked
list: A manual pass with the VoiceOver and NVDA screen readers, in Greek.
A full audit against WCAG 2.2 AA on a sample of pages, including the Greek texts.

feedback.heading: Report a problem
body: If a page or a feature is hard to use, write to the address below: say which page and what blocked you. We answer within one month and, where needed, give you the information in another form. If you are not satisfied with the answer, you can also turn to the Commissioner for Administration and the Protection of Human Rights (Ombudsman), Cyprus’s equality body.

AccessibilityCy.authorityLink: The Commissioner for Administration and the Protection of Human Rights (ombudsman.gov.cy)

DataCy.metaDescription: Where the Cypriot pages of Apercura come from (the Ministry of Health’s open lists on data.gov.cy), under which licence, and how to correct or remove a page.
DataCy.title: Data and sources
DataCy.lead: Every Cypriot page is built from public lists. Here is where the data comes from, under which licence and credit, what is kept and why, when it was updated, and how to correct or remove a page.

status.heading: Last update
status.body: The Pharmaceutical Services update their list of private pharmacies once a year; the lists of state hospitals and state health centres were last published in 2018 and may be out of date. The directory reads every list once a month: a page changes only when its facts change in the list.
status.notImported: The Cypriot directory has not been imported yet on this site.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.body: Every list is published on the national open data portal (data.gov.cy) under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Each credit below is printed word for word.
sources.caption: Data sources of the Cypriot directory

cy-farmakeia.use: Private pharmacies: the address, the town or community, the postcode, the pharmacy’s telephone number and the list’s registration number (ΑΜ). The pharmacist’s name and home telephone number are never read.
cy-farmakeia.frequency: Once a year, by the Pharmaceutical Services

cy-nosokomeia.use: State hospitals: the name, the address, the telephone number and the point of each hospital
cy-nosokomeia.frequency: Irregularly, by the Ministry of Health (list of 2018)

cy-kentra-ygeias.use: State health centres: the name and the telephone number (the list gives no address)
cy-kentra-ygeias.frequency: Irregularly, by the Ministry of Health (list of 2018)

cy-tk.use: The postcodes of every municipality and community, the official Latin form of their names and their centre
cy-tk.frequency: Once a year, by the Department of Postal Services

cy-apografi.use: The municipalities and communities of the areas the census counted, and their population
cy-apografi.frequency: With each census, by the Statistical Service

licence.heading: The licence of the lists
body: The lists are reused under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), which lets anyone copy, share and adapt them, for any purpose, with the credit the licence requires.
list: Attribution (CC BY 4.0, section 3): every page built from a list names its publisher and the licence, links to both and says that Apercura changed the data.
No endorsement (section 2(a)(6)): the pages never present Apercura as approved by the Ministry of Health, the Pharmaceutical Services or any other publisher, and Apercura has no tie with them.

Personal data: the licence does not make personal data free to reuse. The directory never reads the pharmacist’s name or home telephone number the list of private pharmacies gives, and names a pharmacy after its address.
The lists are provided as they are, without warranty (section 5): the facts of a page are the list’s.
licence.changes: A private pharmacy is named after its address (“Φαρμακείο, Ερμού 51Γ, Λάρνακα”), the town repeated at the end of an address dropped; two pharmacies at the same address and postcode are one page. Its telephone number is shown when it is a fixed or business line, not a mobile number. It is placed in the municipality or community of its postcode, else of its town as the list writes it, and shown at that place’s centre (no map pin). A state hospital is placed by the postcode or the place its address names and located at the point the Ministry’s list gives; its web address, from before the state hospitals moved to the State Health Services Organisation, is not shown. A state health centre is placed by the place its name gives (“Κέντρο Υγείας Κοφίνου”) in the district its telephone area code names, and shown at that place’s centre; a centre that names no known place is left out. Names are shown as the lists write them.

coverage.heading: Facilities listed
body: Pages are made for the private pharmacies of the Pharmaceutical Services’ list and for the state hospitals and health centres of the Ministry of Health’s lists, in the five districts of Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca, Paphos and Famagusta, by municipality and community.
The areas of the Republic of Cyprus in which the Government of the Republic of Cyprus does not exercise effective control are not covered: no open source publishes the facilities there.

Not listed either, because no open list of them is published: private clinics and hospitals, doctors, dentists and the other health professionals, laboratories, and the personal doctors of the General Healthcare System (GHS).

A pharmacy or a health centre is shown at the centre of its municipality or community: its map position and its distance are then those of the place, never of the address. A hospital is shown at the point the Ministry’s list gives.

identifiers.heading: Identifiers
body: The address of every page ends with a key, so that the page can be found and checked:
list: /cy/monada/farmakeio-ermou-51g-larnaka-f1197: a private pharmacy, and after the letter f its registration number (ΑΜ) in the Pharmaceutical Services’ list.

/cy/monada/geniko-nosokomeio-lefkosias-m3fa9c01b2e: a state hospital or health centre. The Ministry’s lists number none, so the key after the letter m is derived from the facility’s kind and name: a renamed facility gets a new page.
No person’s identity card number is ever used.

correct.heading: Correct an error
body: The pages repeat the lists: a lasting correction is made at the source, and the page follows at the next import.
For anything else, use the form: we check every report.
list: A pharmacy reports a change of address or telephone number to the Pharmaceutical Services of the Ministry of Health, which keep the list of private pharmacies.
A state hospital or health centre reports its change to the Ministry of Health, which publishes the lists on data.gov.cy.
correct.formBody: Give the address of the page and what is wrong.

remove.heading: Remove a page
body: Anyone a page concerns can object to its publication at any time, without giving a reason (GDPR article 21). An unclaimed page is hidden as soon as the request arrives and deleted after a light check; it never comes back with the updates of the lists. A claimed page is removed by its holder, from their space.
remove.formTitle: Ask for a page to be removed
remove.formBody: Give the address of the page and an e-mail address where we can answer you.
